related_questions.question: Does Medicare pay for a motorized wheelchair?

text_blocks.snippet: Medicare Part B may cover motorized wheelchairs (also called power wheelchairs or power-operated vehicles) if they are deemed medically necessary for use within the home. To qualify, you'll need a face-to-face examination by a doctor, a written prescription, and documentation showing limited mobility and an inability to perform daily living activities even with other mobility aids like canes, crutches, or walkers. Medicare also requires that the wheelchair be used safely within the home and that the supplier accepts Medicare assignment.
snippet_highlighted_words: Medicare Part B may cover motorized wheelchairs (also called power wheelchairs or power-operated vehicles) if they are deemed medically necessary for use within the home

list.snippet: Medicare covers power wheelchairs as Durable Medical Equipment (DME).
You must have a medical condition that significantly limits your ability to move around in your home and perform essential daily tasks like bathing, dressing, or using the bathroom.
A face-to-face examination with your doctor is required to establish medical necessity.
The doctor must document that you can't safely and effectively use a cane, crutch, or walker to move around your home.
Medicare Part B covers 80% of the approved cost of the wheelchair after you've met your annual deductible.
You are responsible for the remaining 20%.
Prior authorization may be required for certain power wheelchairs.
Medicare may also cover rentals for a period of time, and in some cases, the rental period can lead to ownership.
The wheelchair must be usable within your home, and the supplier must verify that your home environment is suitable for its use.
You must be able to safely operate the wheelchair, or have someone available to assist you.
Medicare generally only covers one wheelchair or scooter at a time, and replacements are usually only allowed every five years unless there are specific circumstances.
Make sure your DME supplier accepts Medicare assignment, as this ensures you'll pay the lowest cost.
You may need to provide documentation to Medicare, including a prescription and medical records from your doctor within 45 days of the face-to-face consultation.
